The only generic `/ws/rest/v1` code that calls `LocationService.saveLocation` is in `openmrs-module-webservices.rest`. Three production call sites are affected, and one test file also calls it.

1. **`LocationResource1_8.save`** (`openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_8/LocationResource1_8.java:218-224`). This is the generic `location` resource's save hook. It is the path used by REST create and update of locations, through `DelegatingCrudResource`.
2. **`LocationAttributeResource1_9.save`** (`openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/resource/openmrs1_9/LocationAttributeResource1_9.java:85-103`). It adds the attribute to its parent location and then calls `saveLocation` on that location. This is the create and update path for location attributes.
3. **`LocationAttributeResource1_9.delete`** (same file, `:109-114`). It voids the attribute and then calls `saveLocation` on the parent location, so a change in `saveLocation` affects attribute deletes too.
4. **`LocationController1_9Test`** (`openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod/src/test/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/v1_0/controller/openmrs1_9/LocationController1_9Test.java:164, 225, 242`). This is a test-only caller. It would show a regression first if `saveLocation` behaviour changed.

Inside `openmrs-core`, `saveLocation` is called from `LocationServiceImpl` (lines 260 and 269) and from the core test suite, but those are not in the REST module. The core-side method definitions are `api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/LocationService.java:68`, `api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/impl/LocationServiceImpl.java:67`, and `api/src/main/java/org/openmrs/api/db/hibernate/HibernateLocationDAO.java:56`.

I checked only the `.java` files in the REST module with the reference search and a grep for `saveLocation(`. I did not open the other REST resource classes, so a caller that reaches `saveLocation` through a different wrapper would not show up here.
